<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In May 2016, the Company implemented the 2016
Employee Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) for employees and reserved 818,181 shares of Class A Voting Common Stock for issuance
under the Plan. The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors amended the stock option Plan to reduce the number of authorized options from <span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance_c20160531__us-gaap--PlanNameAxis__custom--N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember_pd" title="Shares reserved for future issuance"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="AsOf2016-05-31_custom_N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember" id="Fact001479" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">818,181</ix:nonFraction></span>
to <span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance_c20201202__us-gaap--PlanNameAxis__custom--N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember_pd" title="Shares reserved for future issuance"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="AsOf2020-12-02_custom_N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember" id="Fact001481" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">733,424</ix:nonFraction></span> per the terms of the December 2, 2020, stock purchase and exchange agreement. As of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, there
remains <span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant_c20260630__us-gaap--PlanNameAxis__custom--N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember_pd" title="Shares available"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" contextRef="AsOf2026-06-30_custom_N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember" id="Fact001483" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">135,924</ix:nonFraction></span> and <span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant_c20251231__us-gaap--PlanNameAxis__custom--N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember_pd" title="Shares available"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31_custom_N2016EmployeeStockIncentivePlanMember" id="Fact001485" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">175,924</ix:nonFraction></span> shares, respectively, available for issuance under the Plan.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8AE_z5S9LLK72Zde" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company uses the Black-Scholes option-pricing
model to estimate the grant date fair value of stock options, which requires the use of assumptions, including the expected term of the
option, expected volatility of its stock price, and the risk-free interest rate, among others. These assumptions reflect best estimates,
however; they involve inherent uncertainties including market conditions and employee behavior that are generally outside of the Company&#8217;s
control. Generally, once stock option values are determined, accounting practices do not permit them to be changed, even if the estimates
used are different from actual results. All stock-based compensation is expensed when awarded to employees based on the grant date fair
value of the awards over the requisite service period, adjusted for forfeitures. Stock-based compensation expense was $<span id="xdx_905_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation_c20260401__20260630_pp0p" title="Stock-based compensation expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2026-04-012026-06-30" id="Fact001545" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">51,151</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation_c20260101__20260630_pp0p" title="Stock-based compensation expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001547" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">91,197</ix:nonFraction></span>
for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, and $<span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation_c20250401__20250630_pp0p" title="Stock-based compensation expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2025-04-012025-06-30" id="Fact001549" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">0</ix:nonFraction></span> and $<span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation_c20250101__20250630_pp0p" title="Stock-based compensation expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EmployeeBenefitsAndShareBasedCompensation" contextRef="From2025-01-012025-06-30" id="Fact001551" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">20,974</ix:nonFraction></span> for the three and six months ended June 30, 2025, respectively.
The intrinsic value of the options outstanding as of June 30, 2026, was $<span id="xdx_902_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingIntrinsicValue_c20260630_pp0p" title="Intrinsic value of options outstanding"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingIntrinsicValue" contextRef="AsOf2026-06-30" id="Fact001553" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">2,743</ix:nonFraction></span> with an unamortized compensation expense of $<span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized_iI_pp0d_c20260630_z793whC6wNH5" title="Unamortized compensation expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" contextRef="AsOf2026-06-30" id="Fact001555" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">450,780</ix:nonFraction></span> to
be recorded over the next five years.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A3_zPNIFykesJL5" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Stock compensation is included in general and
administrative expense in the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated statements of and comprehensive income (loss).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has a Long-Term Incentive Plan
that sets aside 5% of net proceeds from a liquidity event to be paid to the Company&#8217;s employees.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" escape="true" id="Fact001626" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock"><p id="xdx_809_eus-gaap--EarningsPerShareTextBlock_zFxbSIcJod2f" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 9: <span id="xdx_82D_zDQv8lFUyxm2">NET INCOME (LOSS) PER SHARE</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Basic net income (loss) per share is computed
by dividing net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders for the period by the weighted average shares of common stock outstanding
during each period. Diluted net income, when applicable, per share is computed by dividing net income attributable to common stockholders
for the period by the weighted average shares of common stock, common stock equivalents and potentially dilutive securities outstanding
during each period. The Company uses the treasury stock method to determine whether there is a dilutive effect of outstanding option grants.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The reconciliations for the numerator and denominator for net
loss attributable to common stockholders are as follows:</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" escape="true" id="Fact001706" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80E_eus-gaap--IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock_zinvKk8VdEy6" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 10: <span id="xdx_829_zWW6D9s04bm9">INCOME TAX</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company accounts for income taxes under ASC
Topic 740 &#8211; Income Taxes. Under this standard, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for future tax benefits or consequences
attributable to temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective
tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in
which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s tax provision for interim
periods is determined using an estimate of the annual effective income tax rate, adjusted for discrete items, if any, that occur in the
relevant period. Each quarter the annual effective rate is updated, and if the estimated tax rate changes, a cumulative adjustment is
made. Income tax expense of $<span id="xdx_905_eus-gaap--IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit_c20260101__20260630_pp0p" title="Income tax expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001708" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">434,545</ix:nonFraction></span> for the six months ended June 30, 2026 &#160;&#160;resulted in an effective income tax rate of <span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations_c20260101__20260630_pd" title="Effective income tax rate"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001710" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Ratio">28.82</ix:nonFraction>%</span>.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s projected effective income
tax rate excluding the impact, if any, of discrete items is <span id="xdx_907_ecustom--EffectiveIncomeTaxRateExcludingImpact_c20260101__20260630_pd" title="Effective income tax rate excluding the impact"><ix:nonFraction name="xero:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateExcludingImpact" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001712" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Ratio">24.43</ix:nonFraction>%</span>, which is higher than the U.S. federal statutory rate of <span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate_c20260101__20260630_pd" title="U.S. federal statutory rate"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001714" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Ratio">21</ix:nonFraction>%</span> primarily
due to net CFC tested income and state taxes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is not presently subject to any income
tax audit in any taxing jurisdiction.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" escape="true" id="Fact001716" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_807_eus-gaap--CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock_zPUgVD6IlJGe" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 11: <span id="xdx_825_zGhZ148kVMK6">CONTINGENCIES</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In the normal course of business, the Company
may become involved in legal proceedings and claims. In accordance with ASC 450, Contingencies, the Company accrues a liability for such
matters when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. When a range of
reasonably possible loss exists, the Company accrues the most probable amount within the range. If no amount within the range is a better
estimate than any other amount, the minimum amount in the range is accrued. Such accruals may include estimates of potential damages,
external legal fees, and other directly related costs expected to be incurred.&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Legal Proceedings</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Tazinique Echols v. Feel the World, Inc. (pre-litigation
ADA demand):</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On January 20, 2026, Feel the World, Inc. received
a pre-suit demand letter from Equal Access Law Group PLLC on behalf of&#160;Tazinique&#160;Echols, a visually impaired individual, alleging
that accessibility barriers on xeroshoes.com violated Title III of the ADA by preventing her from completing an online purchase; the letter
states an intent to seek injunctive relief, statutory damages where available, interest, and attorneys&#8217; fees if litigation is filed,
and offers to resolve the matter in exchange for remediation of the website and a $15,000.00 dollar payment and release. On June 1, 2026, the Company entered into a settlement agreement for $10,000 and the matter has been closed.</p>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"></p>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Anthony Devies v. Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a
Xero Shoes (threatened TCPA class action):&#160;&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On October 26, 2025, the class action firm Shamis
&amp; Gentile, P.A. sent a certified-mail demand letter to Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a Xero Shoes asserting that automated telemarketing
text messages were sent from short code 65099 to consumer Anthony Devies&#8217;cellular telephone without prior express consent and despite
his registration on the National Do Not Call Registry, and stating that, absent a response by November 16, 2025, counsel will pursue a
putative class action under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act seeking monetary and injunctive relief. As of March 17, 2026, Feel The
World, Inc.'s attorney filed a motion-to-dismiss and the Plaintiff&#8217;s opposition briefing is still to come.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Leon Weingrad v. Feel the World, Inc.&#160;
</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">A putative class action was filed on January 1,
2026, alleging violations of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) for sending unsolicited marketing text messages to individuals
on the Do-Not-Call Registry and/or after opt-out requests.&#160; The Company has filed a motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations.
&#160;In response, the plaintiff filed an amended complaint, and the Company filed another motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations,
which remains pending. &#160;No settlement discussions have occurred, and the plaintiff has not provided a demand.&#160; It is too early
to determine the outcome, and the probability of loss cannot be assessed at this stage (neither probable nor remote).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2026, the Company has not
recorded any accruals for loss contingencies. While certain threatened litigation matters exist, these matters are in the early
stages, and management is unable to determine whether a loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to reasonably estimate the
amount or range of potential loss, if any. Accordingly, no provision has been recorded in the accompanying condensed consolidated
financial statements. The Company will continue to evaluate these matters as additional information becomes available.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i></i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Tariff Refunds</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Beginning in early 2025, additional tariffs
were imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (&#8220;IEEPA&#8221;) on products imported by the Company. In February
2026, the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated certain tariffs imposed under IEEPA, and in March 2026 the U.S. Court of International Trade
ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection to suspend collection of the invalidated tariffs and to establish a process to refund IEEPA
tariffs previously collected. During the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company received refunds of $<span id="xdx_904_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260401__20260630_pp0p" title="Refund received"><span id="xdx_907_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260101__20260630_pp0p" title="Refund received"><ix:nonFraction name="xero:RefundReceived" contextRef="From2026-04-012026-06-30" id="Fact001718" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD"><ix:nonFraction name="xero:RefundReceived" contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" id="Fact001720" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">49,374</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span></span> of previously
paid IEEPA tariffs related to products sold in prior periods, which were recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue. Subsequent to June
30, 2026, the Company received additional refunds of $<span id="xdx_906_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260701__20260928__us-gaap--SubsequentEventTypeAxis__us-gaap--SubsequentEventMember_pp0p" title="Refund received"><ix:nonFraction name="xero:RefundReceived" contextRef="From2026-07-012026-09-28_us-gaap_SubsequentEventMember" id="Fact001722" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="0" unitRef="USD">1,823,401</ix:nonFraction></span>. Consistent with the manner in which the related tariffs were originally
recorded, refunds of tariffs on products that have been sold are recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue, and refunds of tariffs
on products remaining in inventory are recorded as a reduction of the cost of that inventory and are recognized in cost of revenue as
the related products are sold.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2026-01-01to2026-06-30" escape="true" id="Fact001726" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80B_eus-gaap--SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock_z7WbK1EkHY6c" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 12: <span id="xdx_82E_zpKYc72Rq2Bl">SEGMENT REPORTING</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In November 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-07
Segment Reporting (Topic 280): <i>&#8220;Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures to enhance the reportable segment disclosures.&#8221;</i>
The guidance requires additional disclosures about significant segment expenses.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As noted above, the Company is footwear brand
focusing on natural movement, quality craftsmanship, and affordability. Xero Shoes&#174; product lines currently include minimalist casual
and performance shoes, boots, and sandals, as well as do-it-yourself (DIY) sandal kits. Its products are sold directly to customers through
its own website, via third party sites such as Amazon, in certain retail stores, and to international wholesale and distribution partners.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company generates revenues in two business
segments: (1) the North American operations which includes all foreign distributors outside of European operations, and (2) European operations which
includes the European Union countries and the Middle Eastern wholesale accounts. The Company primarily sells through three channels: direct-to-consumer,
third-party platforms such as Amazon, and wholesale/distribution.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer is
the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;). The CODM manages the Company&#8217;s business activities as multiple operating
and reportable segments. The CODM uses consolidated profit and loss to evaluate and measure performance.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><span id="a_008"></span><b>ITEM 2. MANAGEMENT&#8217;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL
CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The following discussion and analysis of
our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements
and the related notes included elsewhere in this Quarterly Report, and with our audited consolidated financial statements and related
notes and the information under the heading &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221;
included in our Registration Statement on Form 10. In addition to historical information, the following discussion contains forward-looking
statements that reflect our plans, estimates, and beliefs. Our actual results could differ materially from those discussed in the forward-looking
statements. See &#8220;Forward-Looking Statements&#8221; and &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8221; for a discussion of the uncertainties,
risks, and assumptions associated with these statements. The components of our results of operations are described in our Registration
Statement on Form 10 and have not materially changed.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Business Overview</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Feel The World, Inc., doing business as Xero
Shoes&#174;, is a designer and marketer of minimalist, natural-movement footwear, including performance and casual shoes, boots, sandals,
and do-it-yourself sandal kits, sold under the Xero Shoes&#174; brand. The Company sells its products through direct-to-consumer e-commerce,
wholesale accounts and independent international distributors, and third-party marketplaces. The Company reports revenue across two operating
segments: North American operations, which includes all foreign distributors outside of Europe, and European operations, which includes
the European Union countries and Middle Eastern wholesale accounts. The Company&#8217;s business is seasonal, with a higher proportion
of revenue and operating cash flow generated during the second half of the calendar year.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s business is subject to
an evolving macroeconomic and trade environment, including changes in tariffs. Beginning in early 2025, significant additional tariffs
were imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (&#8220;IEEPA&#8221;) on products imported from various countries,
including the countries in which the Company&#8217;s products are manufactured. In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated certain
tariffs imposed under IEEPA, and in March 2026 the U.S. Court of International Trade ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection to suspend
collection of the invalidated tariffs and to establish a process to refund IEEPA tariffs previously collected. As a result, the Company
is eligible to receive refunds of tariffs previously paid on qualifying imports. During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company
received $49,374 of such refunds, which related to products sold in prior periods and was recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue.
Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the Company received an additional $1,823,401 of such refunds. There remains substantial uncertainty regarding
potential changes to existing and newly announced tariffs, whether additional tariffs may be imposed, modified, or suspended, and the
timing of any refunds, any of which could materially and adversely affect the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, and results
of operations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During the second quarter of 2026, the Company&#8217;s
revenue increased 14.7% over the second quarter of 2025, driven by growth in its direct-to-consumer and wholesale and distributor channels,
partially offset by lower European revenue. Gross margin expanded to 51.6% of revenue from 47.1%, reflecting a higher proportion of full-price
sales relative to the prior-year period, partially offset by higher fulfillment costs. Income from operations improved to $885,930 from
$83,735 in the prior-year quarter. Net income of $600,393 compared to $943,385 in the prior-year quarter, which included a $406,719 gain
on the reversal of a loss on settlement and a $675,424 income tax benefit, neither of which recurred in the current period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Revenue</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Revenue for the three months ended June 30,
2026 was $16,908,295, an increase of $2,171,794, or 14.7%, compared to $14,736,501 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase
reflected higher direct-to-consumer volume on the Company&#8217;s 2026 product line, a full quarter of sales through the Company&#8217;s
marketplace distributor partner compared to a prior-year quarter that was disrupted by the transition of the Company&#8217;s third-party
marketplace business to that partner, and sales to distributor partners added in international markets over the past year, partially offset
by lower European revenue. The current period also reflected a higher proportion of full-price direct-to-consumer sales, whereas the prior-year
period included a greater proportion of inventory-liquidation and clearance-related sales, which contributed to improved realized pricing
and gross margin, as discussed below. Growth in gross product sales was partially offset at the net revenue level by higher discounts
and customer returns associated with the increased direct-to-consumer volume.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">By geographic segment, North American revenue
increased $2,979,317, or 27.2%, to $13,939,301 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $10,959,984 for the
three months ended June 30, 2025, driven by the recovery in marketplace sales following the prior-year transition to the distributor model,
new international distributor relationships, and full-price direct-to-consumer growth. European revenue decreased $807,523, or 21.4%,
to $2,968,994 from $3,776,517, reflecting the wind-down of the Company&#8217;s United Kingdom direct operations, which contributed
$549,548 of revenue in the prior-year quarter, lower European wholesale revenue as certain European retailers experienced financial difficulty
and reduced their inventory commitments, lower European direct-to-consumer promotional activity, and the effect of foreign currency translation.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 32 -->
    <div style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 9pt; width: 100%"><tr><td style="text-align: center; width: 100%"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->29<!-- Field: /Sequence -->&#160;</td></tr></table></div>
    <div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%"><tr><td style="text-align: center; width: 100%">&#160;</td></tr></table></div>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Gross product sales (before returns, discounts,
and shipping revenue) were $19,285,429 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $16,696,577 for the three months ended June
30, 2025. Customer returns, allowances, and chargebacks decreased to $1,839,852 from $2,078,593, reflecting the shift in the Company&#8217;s
sales mix toward wholesale and distributor partners, which generate fewer returns than direct-to-consumer sales, and changes to the Company&#8217;s
direct-to-consumer return policy. Discounts increased to $956,245 from $279,981, reflecting increased promotional discounting in the current
period. Shipping revenue billed to customers, which is included in revenue, increased to $418,963 from $398,498, reflecting higher order
volume, partially offset by the Company&#8217;s continued use of free-shipping promotions.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Cost of Revenues</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Cost of revenue for the three months ended
June 30, 2026 was $8,187,623, an increase of $390,915, or 5.0%, compared to $7,796,708 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Cost
of revenue consisted of $5,943,978 of product cost in the 2026 period, compared to $5,862,348 in the 2025 period, and $2,243,645 of fulfillment
cost in the 2026 period, compared to $1,934,360 in the 2025 period. Product cost increased 1.4% on revenue growth of 14.7%, reflecting
the improvement in realized pricing described above, while fulfillment cost increased 16.0%, reflecting higher direct-to-consumer unit
volume and returns and higher shipping costs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Gross profit for the three months ended June
30, 2026 was $8,720,672, or 51.6% of revenue, compared to $6,939,793, or 47.1% of revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an
increase of $1,780,879, or 25.7%, and gross-margin expansion of approximately 4.5 percentage points. The improvement in gross margin primarily
reflected a higher proportion of full-price sales and reduced inventory-liquidation activity relative to the prior-year period, partially
offset by higher fulfillment costs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Operating Expenses</i>. Total operating expenses for the three months
ended June 30, 2026 were $7,834,742, an increase of $978,684, or 14.5%, compared to $6,856,058 for the three months ended June 30, 2025.
The increase primarily reflected higher sales and marketing expense and higher operations expense, partially offset by lower general and
administrative expense.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>General and Administrative. </i>General
and administrative expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $1,730,675, a decrease of $125,071, or 6.7%, compared to $1,855,746
for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease primarily reflected the absence of restructuring-related costs incurred in the
prior-year period in connection with the Company&#8217;s 2025 workforce reductions, partially offset by higher professional, legal, audit,
and compliance costs, including costs associated with the Company becoming a reporting company under the Exchange Act.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Sales and Marketing. </i>Sales and marketing
expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $4,551,367, an increase of $854,191, or 23.1%, compared to $3,697,176 for the three
months ended June 30, 2025. Sales and marketing expense as a percentage of revenue was 26.9% in the 2026 period compared to 25.1% in the
2025 period. The increase reflected higher advertising and marketing expense, higher sales commissions as a greater proportion of the
Company&#8217;s European wholesale accounts are serviced by independent sales agencies rather than in-house sales personnel, and higher
selling costs associated with the increased direct-to-consumer volume.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Research and Development. </i>Research
and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $428,246, an increase of $17,893, or 4.4%, compared to $410,353
for the three months ended June 30, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Operations. </i>Operations expenses for
the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $1,124,454, an increase of $231,671, or 25.9%, compared to $892,783 for the three months ended
June 30, 2025. The increase primarily reflected higher costs associated with increased unit volume and severance costs incurred during
the period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Income from Operations</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result of the foregoing, the Company generated
income from operations of $885,930 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to income from operations of $83,735 for the three
months ended June 30, 2025, an improvement of $802,195.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Total other income (expense), net for the three
months ended June 30, 2026 was an expense of $37,115, compared to income of $184,226 for the three months ended June 30, 2025, an unfavorable
change of $221,341. The change primarily reflected the absence in the 2026 period of a $406,719 gain recognized in the prior-year period
on the reversal of a previously recorded loss on settlement, partially offset by lower interest expense.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Interest Expense. </i>Interest expense for
the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $102,818, a decrease of $8,467, or 7.6%, compared to $111,285 for the three months ended June
30, 2025, reflecting lower average outstanding borrowings under the Company&#8217;s credit facilities during the 2026 period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Loss on Settlement. </i>There was no loss on
settlement for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The three months ended June 30, 2025 included a $406,719 gain reflecting the reversal
of a loss on settlement that had been recorded in the three months ended March 31, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Other Income (Expense). </i>Other income (expense),
net was income of $65,521 &#160;for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a net expense of $111,208 for the three months ended
June 30, 2025. The change primarily reflected fluctuations in foreign currency transaction gains and losses.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Provision for (Benefit from) Income Taxes</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recorded a provision for income taxes
of $248,422 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a benefit from income tax of $675,424 for the three months ended
June 30, 2025. The provision for the 2026 period reflects the application of the Company&#8217;s estimated annual effective tax rate to
pre-tax income, taking into account the Company&#8217;s valuation allowance position, and represents an effective tax rate of 29.27%.
The benefit in the prior-year period reflected the Company&#8217;s pre-tax results and interim tax accounting for that period and did
not recur.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Net Income (Loss)</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result of the foregoing, the Company
recorded net income of $600,393 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to net income of $943,385 for the three months ended
June 30, 2025, a decrease of $342,992. The decrease occurred notwithstanding the $802,195 improvement in income from operations, because
the prior-year period included a $406,719 gain on the reversal of a loss on settlement and an income tax benefit of $675,424, neither
of which recurred in the 2026 period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Revenue</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026
was $32,891,465, an increase of $2,923,686, or 9.8%, compared to $29,967,779 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase reflected
growth in the Company&#8217;s North American operations, driven by a full period of sales through the Company&#8217;s marketplace distributor
partner, sales to distributor partners added in international markets, and higher direct-to-consumer volume, partially offset by lower
European revenue; wholesale revenue was essentially unchanged as new-season bookings offset lower European wholesale volume. The comparability
of revenue between the two periods was also affected by shifts in the Company&#8217;s sales mix. The prior-year period included first-party
sales through a third-party marketplace during the first quarter of 2025, substantially all of which had transitioned to sales through
a distributor partner beginning in April 2025; the Company records sales to that distributor partner within its wholesale and distributor
channel. In addition, the prior-year period reflected a higher proportion of inventory-liquidation and clearance-related direct-to-consumer
sales, whereas the current period reflected a greater proportion of full-price sales, which contributed to improved realized pricing and
gross margin, as discussed below.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">By geographic segment, North American revenue
increased $4,488,768, &#160;or 20.5%, to $26,392,988 &#160;for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $21,904,220 &#160;for the six months
ended June 30, 2025, driven by the recovery in marketplace sales following the prior-year transition to the distributor model, new international
distributor relationships, and direct-to-consumer growth. European revenue decreased $1,565,082, or 19.4%, to $6,498,477 &#160;from $8,063,559,
reflecting the wind-down of the Company&#8217;s United Kingdom direct operations, which contributed $874,692 of revenue in the prior-year
period, lower European wholesale revenue as certain European retailers experienced financial difficulty and reduced their inventory commitments,
lower European direct-to-consumer promotional activity, and the effect of foreign currency translation.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Gross product sales (before returns, discounts,
and shipping revenue) were $37,084,171 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $34,098,687 &#160;for the six months ended
June 30, 2025. Customer returns, allowances, and chargebacks decreased to $3,155,825 from $4,328,449, reflecting the shift in the Company&#8217;s
sales mix toward wholesale and distributor partners, which generate fewer returns than direct-to-consumer sales, and changes to the Company&#8217;s
direct-to-consumer return policy. Discounts increased to $1,698,759 from $789,441, reflecting differences in the nature of promotional
activity between the periods. Shipping revenue billed to customers, which is included in revenue, decreased to $661,878 from $986,982,
reflecting the Company&#8217;s continued use of free-shipping promotions.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Cost of Revenues</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Cost of revenue for the six months ended
June 30, 2026 was $16,525,207, a decrease of $169,396, or 1.0%, compared to $16,694,603 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Cost of
revenue consisted of $12,427,106 of product cost in the 2026 period, compared to $12,608,869 in the 2025 period, and $4,098,101 of fulfillment
cost in the 2026 period, compared to $4,085,734 in the 2025 period. Product cost decreased 1.4% on revenue growth of 9.8%, reflecting
the improvement in realized pricing described above, while fulfillment cost was essentially unchanged.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Gross profit for the six months ended June
30, 2026 was $16,366,258, or 49.8% of revenue, compared to $13,273,176, or 44.3% of revenue, for the six months ended June 30, 2025, an
increase of $3,093,082, or 23.3%, and gross-margin expansion of approximately 5.5 percentage points. The improvement in gross margin primarily
reflected a higher proportion of full-price sales and reduced inventory-liquidation activity relative to the prior-year period, together
with a more favorable channel mix that carried lower fulfillment costs and lower return rates.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Operating Expenses</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Total operating expenses for the six months
ended June 30, 2026 were $14,682,966, an increase of $710,530, or 5.1%, compared to $13,972,436 for the six months ended June 30, 2025.
The increase reflected higher sales and marketing expense in the second quarter and higher research and development expense, partially
offset by the full-period benefit of the workforce reductions and organizational restructuring completed during the first half of 2025
and the transition of the Company&#8217;s third-party marketplace business to a distributor model, which shifted the related fulfillment,
advertising, and marketing costs to the distributor partner.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i></i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>General and Administrative. </i>General and
administrative expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $3,250,373, a decrease of $41,203, or 1.3%, compared to $3,291,576
for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Higher professional, audit, and compliance costs associated with the Company becoming a reporting
company under the Exchange Act were more than offset by the absence of restructuring-related costs incurred in the prior-year period.</p>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Sales and Marketing. </i>Sales and marketing
expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $8,301,529, an increase of $616,795, or 8.0%, compared to $7,684,734 for the six
months ended June 30, 2025. Sales and marketing expense as a percentage of revenue was 25.2% in the 2026 period compared to 25.6% in the
2025 period. The increase in expense reflected higher advertising and marketing expense in the second quarter and higher sales commissions
as a greater proportion of the Company&#8217;s European wholesale accounts are serviced by independent sales agencies rather than in-house
sales personnel.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Research and Development. </i>Research
and development expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $968,731, an increase of $158,008, or 19.5%, compared to $810,723
for the six months ended June 30, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Operations. </i>Operations expenses for
the six months ended June 30, 2026 were $2,162,333, a decrease of $23,070, or 1.1%, compared to $2,185,403 for the six months ended June
30, 2025, as lower costs in the first quarter were largely offset by higher volume-related costs and severance in the second quarter.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Income (Loss) from Operations</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result of the foregoing, the Company generated
income from operations of $1,683,292 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a loss from operations of $699,260 for the six
months ended June 30, 2025, an improvement of $2,382,552.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Total other expense, net for the six months ended
June 30, 2026 was $175,751, a decrease of $293,863, or 62.6%, compared to $469,614 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease
was driven primarily by a favorable change in foreign currency transaction gains and losses and lower interest expense.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Interest Expense. </i>Interest expense for
the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $191,609, a decrease of $28,115, or 12.8%, compared to $219,724 for the six months ended June 30,
2025, reflecting lower average outstanding borrowings under the Company&#8217;s credit facilities during the 2026 period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Loss on Settlement. </i>There was no loss on
settlement for the six months ended June 30, 2026 or 2025. The six months ended June 30, 2025 included a $406,719 loss on settlement recorded
in the first quarter of 2025 that was reversed in the second quarter of 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Other Income (Expense). </i>Other income (expense),
net was income of $15,676 &#160;for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a net expense of $249,890 for the six months ended
June 30, 2025. The change primarily reflected fluctuations in foreign currency transaction gains and losses.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Provision for (Benefit from) Income Taxes</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recorded a provision for income taxes
of $434,545 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a benefit from income tax of $400,164 for the six months ended June 30,
2025. The provision for the 2026 period reflects the application of the Company&#8217;s estimated annual effective tax rate to pre-tax
income, taking into account the Company&#8217;s valuation allowance position, and represents an effective tax rate of 28.82%. The
benefit in the prior-year period reflected the pre-tax loss for that period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Net Income (Loss)</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result of the foregoing, the Company recorded
net income of $1,072,996 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $768,710 for the six months ended June 30,
2025, an improvement of $1,841,706.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Liquidity and Capital Resources</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Overview</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has historically funded its operations
through cash generated from operations, borrowings under its credit facilities, and proceeds from the issuance of equity securities. As
of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $6,169,920, compared to $10,134,276 as of December 31, 2025, a decrease
of $3,964,356. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had $2,063,629 outstanding under its revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo, compared
to $4,000,000 outstanding under its revolving credit facility with JPMorgan Chase as of December 31, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In February 2026, the Company entered into
a new credit agreement with Wells Fargo providing for a revolving commitment of $12,000,000 with a maturity date of February 5, 2029.
The Company drew on the new Wells Fargo facility to repay its outstanding revolving commitment with JPMorgan Chase, which had matured
in February 2026, and for working capital purposes, and during the second quarter reduced its outstanding borrowings under the facility
from cash generated by the business. The Wells Fargo facility increased the Company&#8217;s borrowing capacity by $8,000,000 compared
to the prior JPMorgan Chase facility and extended the Company&#8217;s debt maturity profile.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company believes that its current cash
and cash equivalents, anticipated cash flows from operations, and available borrowing capacity under the Wells Fargo credit facility are
sufficient to fund its operations and capital requirements for at least the next twelve months. The Company&#8217;s future liquidity needs
will depend on a number of factors, including the rate of growth in its business, the timing of inventory purchases and other working
capital requirements, capital expenditures, debt service obligations, and the costs and timing of any future strategic initiatives.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Working Capital</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2026, the Company had working capital
of $17,188,710, calculated as total current assets of $31,647,433 less total current liabilities of $14,458,723. This compares to working
capital of $16,425,904 as of December 31, 2025, calculated as total current assets of $36,298,372 less total current liabilities of $19,872,468,
an increase of $762,806. Current assets decreased $4,650,939, primarily reflecting a $3,964,356 decrease in cash and a $1,903,673 decrease
in inventory in transit as in-transit goods were received into inventory, partially offset by increases in prepaid expenses, inventory,
and accounts receivable. Current liabilities decreased $5,413,745, primarily reflecting a $2,925,221 reduction in accounts payable and
accrued expenses, which had been elevated at December 31, 2025 in connection with the timing of inventory receipts and vendor payments,
a $2,143,706 reduction in the net carrying amount of the Company&#8217;s line of credit, and a $417,247 decrease in customer deposits.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Operating Activities</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash used in operating activities for
the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $929,993, compared to net cash provided by operating activities of $287,372 for the six months
ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $1,217,365. The decrease primarily reflected changes in working capital, including a $2,925,221 reduction
in accounts payable and accrued expenses as the Company paid down vendor balances that had been elevated at December 31, 2025, compared
to a $2,067,020 increase in the prior-year period, together with a $394,810 increase in prepaid expenses, a $493,683 increase in inventory,
a $480,844 increase in accounts receivable and a $417,247 decrease in customer deposits. These uses were partially offset by a $1,903,673
decrease in inventory in transit as in-transit goods were received into inventory, and by the Company&#8217;s net income of $1,072,996
for the six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to a net loss of $768,710 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Non-cash items in
the 2026 period included $313,065 deferred taxes, $203,761 of depreciation and amortization, $56,037 of amortization of debt issuance
costs, $91,197 of stock-based compensation, and $29,935 of credit loss expense.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Investing Activities</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash used in investing activities for
the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $383,604, compared to $437,243 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Investing activities in
the 2026 period consisted of $313,256 of purchases of property and equipment and $70,348 of additions to intangible assets. By comparison,
in the 2025 period the Company invested $369,887 in property and equipment and $67,356 in intangible assets.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Financing Activities</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash used in financing activities for
the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $2,199,743, compared to net cash provided by financing activities of $4,659,967 for the six months
ended June 30, 2025. Financing activities in the 2026 period consisted of gross proceeds of $21,444,023, net of borrowing costs, and gross
repayments of $23,643,766 under the Company&#8217;s revolving credit facilities, reflecting the repayment of the $4,000,000 JPMorgan Chase
revolving commitment upon its maturity, borrowings under the new Wells Fargo facility, and subsequent repayments of borrowings under that
facility during the second quarter. Financing activities in the 2025 period consisted primarily of $4,859,967 of net proceeds from the
issuance of Senior Preferred Stock to TZP Group Investments, L.P., partially offset by $200,000 of repayments on the Company&#8217;s term
loan.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company does not have any off-balance
sheet arrangements that have or are reasonably likely to have a current or future material effect on its financial condition, results
of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures, or capital resources.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Indebtedness</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On February 5, 2026, the Company entered into
a credit agreement with Wells Fargo providing for a revolving commitment of $12,000,000 with a maturity date of February 5, 2029. The
Company utilized a portion of the facility to repay its maturing revolving commitment with JPMorgan Chase. As of June 30, 2026, the Company
had $2,063,629 outstanding under the Wells Fargo revolving commitment. Borrowings under the credit agreement are secured
by substantially all of the assets of the Company.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&#8217;s prior credit agreement with
JPMorgan Chase, which included a $4,000,000 revolving commitment, matured in February 2026 and was repaid in full. Total interest expense
was $134,135 &#160;for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $219,724 for the six months ended June 30, 2025.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Lease Obligations</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company leases its corporate office in Broomfield,
Colorado and a warehouse facility in Denver, Colorado, along with certain office equipment, under operating lease agreements. As of June
30, 2026, the Company had operating lease right-of-use assets of $1,824,887 and total operating lease liabilities of $2,013,797, consisting
of $867,393 of current lease liabilities and $1,146,404 of long-term lease liabilities. The Company&#8217;s operating leases
expire at various dates through 2031. See the notes to the condensed consolidated financial statements for additional information regarding
future minimum lease payments.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span id="a_010"></span><b>ITEM 4. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our management, with the participation of
our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined
in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of June 30, 2026, the end of the period covered by this Quarterly Report.
Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of June 30, 2026, due to the material
weakness in our internal control over financial reporting previously identified in Part II, Item 9A of our Annual Report on Form 1-K for
the year ended December 31, 2025, our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective in providing reasonable assurance that information
required to be disclosed in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within
the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms, and is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief
Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.&#160; This material
weakness resulted in the restatements of our financial statements in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q (as to the three and six months
ended June 30, 2025), our Quarterly Financial Statements for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, and our Annual Report on
Form 1-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b><i>Remediation of Material Weakness</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Management has implemented remediation steps
to address the material weakness described above and to improve our internal control over financial reporting. In the third quarter of
2026, we enhanced our processes to strengthen the identification and evaluation of complex accounting matters, including engaging with
independent accounting experts to advise and review complex financial matters, ensuring appropriate technical analysis, documentation,
and oversight prior to the preparation of our financial statements, and strengthening financial disclosure and technical guidance resources.
However, the enhanced controls were not applied to equity instruments issued in prior periods, including the Preferred Stock at issue.
As a result, the classification error was not identified until a subsequent review. Management is in the process of refining these processes
to ensure that previously issued instruments are periodically reassessed in the context of evolving technical guidance and accounting
interpretations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">While the Company&#8217;s remediation process
has been applied in the preparation to these condensed consolidated financial statements, the material weakness cannot be considered fully
remediated until applicable controls have operated for a sufficient period of time and management has concluded, through testing, that
these controls are operating effectively. Accordingly, we will continue to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of our internal control
over financial reporting.</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt/110% Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Other than as described above, there were
no changes in our internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act) during
the quarter ended June 30, 2026 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over
financial reporting.&#160;</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><span id="a_012"></span>ITEM 1. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">From time to time, the Company is involved in
legal proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business. The Company is not currently a party to any legal proceedings that management
believes would, individually or in the aggregate, have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, results of operations,
or cash flows. See <i>Note 11 &#8212; Contingencies to the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Tazinique Echols v. Feel the World, Inc. (pre-litigation
ADA demand):</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On January 20, 2026, Feel the World, Inc. received
a pre-suit demand letter from Equal Access Law Group PLLC on behalf of&#160;Tazinique&#160;Echols, a visually impaired individual, alleging
that accessibility barriers on xeroshoes.com violated Title III of the ADA by preventing her from completing an online purchase; the
letter states an intent to seek injunctive relief, statutory damages where available, interest, and attorneys&#8217; fees if litigation
is filed, and offers to resolve the matter in exchange for remediation of the website and a $15,000.00 dollar payment and release. On
June 1, 2026, the Company entered into a settlement agreement for $10,000 and the matter has been closed.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Anthony Devies v. Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a
Xero Shoes (threatened TCPA class action):&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On October 26, 2025, the class action firm Shamis
&amp; Gentile, P.A. sent a certified-mail demand letter to Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a Xero Shoes asserting that automated telemarketing
text messages were sent from short code 65099 to consumer Anthony Devies&#8217;cellular telephone without prior express consent and despite
his registration on the National Do Not Call Registry, and stating that, absent a response by November 16, 2025, counsel will pursue a
putative class action under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act seeking monetary and injunctive relief. As of March 17, 2026, Feel The
World, Inc.'s attorney filed a motion-to-dismiss and the Plaintiff&#8217;s opposition briefing is still to come.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Leon Weingrad v. Feel the World, Inc.&#160;
</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">A putative class action was filed on January 1,
2026, alleging violations of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) for sending unsolicited marketing text messages to individuals
on the Do-Not-Call Registry and/or after opt-out requests.&#160; The Company has filed a motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations.
&#160;In response, the plaintiff filed an amended complaint, and the Company filed another motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations,
which remains pending. &#160;No settlement discussions have occurred, and the plaintiff has not provided a demand.&#160; It is too early
to determine the outcome, and the probability of loss cannot be assessed at this stage (neither probable nor remote).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">While certain threatened litigation matters
exist, these matters are in the early stages, and management is unable to determine whether a loss is probable or reasonably
possible, or to reasonably estimate the amount or range of potential loss, if any. Accordingly, no provision has been recorded in
the accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements. The Company will continue to evaluate these matters as additional
information becomes available.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>&#160;</i></p>
